items.title: BL-B01D1 Combination Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This is a Phase 2/3 trial testing a new drug combination called BL-B01D1 in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The trial has not started recruiting yet. Details about the specific drugs and mechanism are not provided in the abstract.

items.title: Carboplatin for Metastatic Prostate Cancer with DNA Repair Gene Mutations
items.summary: This completed Phase 2 trial tested whether carboplatin chemotherapy works in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose tumors have mutations in homologous recombination (HR) DNA repair genes. These mutations may make tumors more sensitive to certain chemotherapies. The trial has finished but results are not yet reported.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 for Bone Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial is testing the safety and effectiveness of combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor that blocks DNA repair) with radium-223 (radioactive treatment targeting bone metastases). The trial is no longer recruiting new patients. The combination aims to prevent cancer cells from repairing damage caused by the radioactive treatment.

items.title: Radium-223 with M3814 and Avelumab for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial is actively recruiting patients to compare radium-223 alone versus radium-223 plus M3814 (a drug that blocks DNA repair) versus all three drugs plus avelumab (immunotherapy). The study aims to find the best combination for castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.

items.title: DNA Blood Test Study for High-Volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study in Russia is tracking treatment patterns and testing for DNA repair gene mutations using blood samples (ctDNA) in patients with aggressive, high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will help understand how these patients are treated in real-world settings.

items.title: Dual-Target CAR-NK Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing a novel immunotherapy called ETB-DualNK-01, which uses engineered immune cells (CAR-NK cells) that target two proteins on prostate cancer cells: PSMA and PSCA. The study is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to determine safe dosing and early signs of effectiveness.

items.title: Nivolumab, Ipilimumab, and Cabozantinib for Rare Genitourinary Cancers
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is testing a combination of two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) plus cabozantinib (a targeted therapy) in patients with rare genitourinary tumors that have spread. While prostate cancer may be included, this study focuses on rare tumor types with limited treatment options.

items.title: Lead-212 Targeted Radiotherapy for GRPR-Positive Tumors
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing a radioactive treatment (212Pb-DOTAM-GRPR1) that delivers radiation directly to cancer cells expressing the GRPR protein. The study is recruiting patients with various metastatic cancers including prostate cancer to determine safe dosing and early effectiveness.

items.title: GDC-1261 for Advanced Prostate Cancer Early-Stage Trial
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial is testing a new drug called GDC-1261 in patients with advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to find the safe dose range and look for early signs of effectiveness. Specific details about how the drug works are not provided.

items.title: Combination Radioactive Antibody Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing a combination of two radioactive treatments: 225Ac-J591 (radioactive antibody targeting PSMA) plus 177Lu-PSMA (radioactive small molecule also targeting PSMA). Both deliver radiation directly to prostate cancer cells. The study is recruiting to determine the highest safe dose.

items.title: Tinengotinib Combined with Standard Hormonal Treatments for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial is testing whether adding tinengotinib (TT-00420) to standard hormonal treatments (abiraterone or enzalutamide) is safe and effective in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to determine if this combination improves outcomes over standard treatment alone.

items.title: Pocenbrodib with Darolutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1b/2a trial is testing pocenbrodib alone and in combination with darolutamide (a hormonal therapy) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting to find the right dose and assess safety and early signs of tumor response.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is testing whether adding mevrometostat (an epigenetic drug that blocks a protein called EZH2) to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't received prior hormonal treatments. This is a large, pivotal trial actively recruiting.

items.title: Bipolar Androgen Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing a novel approach called bipolar androgen therapy, which alternates between very low testosterone (castration levels) and very high testosterone (supraphysiological levels). The goal is to suppress cancer growth by rapidly cycling hormone levels, potentially restoring sensitivity to standard hormone treatments.

items.title: Imaging Study of GRPR-Targeted Therapy for Advanced Cancers
items.summary: This Phase 0 imaging study is testing two radioactive tracers (68Ga and 177Lu versions of DOTA-STR-17126) that bind to the GRPR protein on cancer cells. The study includes breast and prostate cancer patients and aims to evaluate safety and imaging quality to support development of a targeted therapy approach.

items.title: JSB462 Safety Study in Japanese Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing the safety and blood levels of JSB462 (luxdegalutamide), a novel hormonal therapy, specifically in Japanese patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will help determine if the drug behaves differently in this population.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone for Hormone-Sensitive Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is testing whether combining luxdegalutamide (JSB462, a novel hormonal drug) with abiraterone works better than standard treatment alone in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will test two different doses to determine the best one for future trials.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy Versus Observation for Limited Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is comparing lutetium-177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto, a radioactive PSMA-targeted therapy) versus observation in patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer (limited number of metastases). The study aims to see if early treatment can prevent progression and delay need for hormone therapy while preserving quality of life. Actively recruiting.

items.title: Multi-Target Radioligand Therapy for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing multiple radioactive treatments targeting different proteins (PSMA, SSTR2, and GRPR) in patients with metastatic neuroendocrine prostate cancer, a rare and aggressive form. The study evaluates how target expression changes after treatment and is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel for Patients with Suboptimal Response to Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is testing whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy helps patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have a suboptimal PSA response to hormone treatment plus androgen receptor inhibitors. The study aims to determine if early chemotherapy can improve outcomes in patients not responding well to initial therapy. Actively recruiting.

items.title: FAPI PET/MRI Imaging Study for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is using a new type of PET scan with FAPI (fibroblast activation protein inhibitor) tracer combined with MRI to better image prostate cancer. The study aims to understand how FAPI binds to cells in the tumor microenvironment, which may improve cancer diagnosis and tracking.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA Plus Hormone Therapy for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is comparing actinium-225 PSMA-617 (a more potent radioactive treatment than lutetium-177) plus hormonal therapy versus standard treatment options in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients previously treated with one hormonal therapy. This is a pivotal trial actively recruiting.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is testing whether adding luxdegalutamide (JSB462, a hormonal drug) to lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy works better than radioligand therapy alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting and will test two different doses of luxdegalutamide.

items.title: QLF4113 Early Phase Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial will test the safety and dosing of QLF4113, a new drug, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The trial has not yet started recruiting. Details about how the drug works are not provided in the abstract.

items.title: Shorter-Course Radiation Therapy for Recurrent Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is testing whether a shorter course of radiation therapy (using either proton beam or standard IMRT) is safe and effective for treating prostate cancer that has come back or spread to a limited number of sites. The trial is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Tulmimetostat with Darolutamide or Abiraterone for Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial is testing two combination approaches: tulmimetostat (an epigenetic drug) plus darolutamide, and tulmimetostat plus abiraterone in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting to evaluate safety and effectiveness of these combinations.

items.title: Opevesostat Versus Alternative Hormone Therapy for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial is comparing opevesostat (a novel drug) versus switching to a different standard hormonal therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have already received one hormonal therapy. This is a pivotal trial actively recruiting.

items.title: AZD6621 Early Testing for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial is testing different delivery methods and doses of AZD6621, a new experimental drug, in adult men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study is recruiting to determine safe dosing and look for early signs of effectiveness.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA Plus Olaparib for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is testing the combination of FPI-2265 (actinium-225 PSMA radioligand therapy) with olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting and aims to optimize dosing of this combination approach.

items.title: HER2-Targeted Therapy Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed Phase 2 trial tested whether adding HER2-targeted therapies (pertuzumab and trastuzumab) to enzalutamide works in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. These drugs target the HER2 protein sometimes found on prostate cancer cells. Results are not yet available.

items.title: Inflammation Drives Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation, through NFκB and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways, changes the genetic and epigenetic landscape of prostate cancer, promoting progression to castration-resistant disease. These inflammatory pathways interact with androgen receptor signaling to drive tumor survival, growth, immune evasion, and metastasis. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to new treatment strategies targeting inflammation.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study tested a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein on prostate cancer cells) and found it generated strong immune responses. When combined with PD-1 immunotherapy blockade, the vaccine increased tumor elimination and prevented lung metastases in animal models, while reducing suppressive immune cells.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Resistance in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This laboratory study developed a novel drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins to overcome resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. When AKT inhibitors are used alone, tumors often develop resistance through increased c-MYC expression; this dual inhibitor addresses both pathways and showed promising results in preclinical models.

items.title: International Comparison of Cancer Drug Reimbursement and Clinical Benefit
items.summary: This study analyzed drug approval and reimbursement patterns for prostate, kidney, and bladder cancers across eight countries (2005-2024). Canada and France had the highest reimbursement rates for prostate cancer drugs (85%), while rates varied significantly by country and tumor type. The study assessed whether drugs providing substantial clinical benefit were more likely to be reimbursed.

items.title: Machine Learning Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: This study developed machine learning models using data from 3,378 prostate cancer patients with bone metastases to predict overall survival. The best model (Extra Survival Trees) identified Gleason score as the most important survival factor, more important than cancer stage. The findings suggest doctors should prioritize aggressive treatment for high-Gleason score patients with high disease burden.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 trials involving 1,580 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors showed modest overall benefits (63% 1-year survival, 39% 2-year survival). Combination therapy with immunotherapy plus other agents showed better outcomes than immunotherapy alone. Results suggest encouraging but preliminary signs for combination approaches.

items.title: Quantum Dot Sensor for Simultaneous Detection of Multiple Tumor Markers
items.summary: This laboratory study developed a highly sensitive fluorescence-based test that can simultaneously detect multiple tumor markers (PSA and AFP) in a single sample. The technology uses quantum dots and may improve early cancer detection, though this is a technical development study not directly testing patient outcomes.

items.title: Bone Health Effects of Enzalutamide Plus Zoledronic Acid Study
items.summary: The BonEnza Phase 2 trial found that adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening drug) to androgen deprivation therapy plus enzalutamide significantly improved bone mineral density and bone quality scores in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients. Without zoledronic acid, patients experienced significant bone loss after 18 months of treatment.
